parsed.explanation: The combined regime layers a hostile national framework over one of the harshest subnational laws in the record. Visitor-facing exposures are documented and universal: passport sex-marker restrictions and a visa-adjudication cable that treats document discrepancy as potential fraud with lifetime-ineligibility findings; foreign governments' advisories follow documented detentions of their trans citizens. The division adds birth-sex confinement in all public buildings including airports, criminal and civil penalties, bounty suits by any private person, and invalidation of licences — no remedy is shown operating, and a documented arrest occurred. Custody exposure (immigration detention abuse) is severe. Partial protections exist (national hate-crime statute, division non-discrimination law, pending litigation) but are not shown remedying the operative exposures. This sits at the harsher edge of the 0.35 anchor tier.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport/visa policy restricts markers to birth sex; cable directs refusal where sex is doubted and considers fraud findings; documented detentions of foreign trans citizens and passports blocked, leaving travellers stranded; trans-athlete entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; litigation pending; foreign consular advisories.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening interacts with division licence invalidation and facility rules at airports — document scrutiny compounds facility exposure at the travel hub itself.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy mandates stripping hormones and hair-cutting; immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, sexual abuse of trans men; bathroom-law arrest produced 24h men's-ward holding.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A facility complaint or bounty suit could route a visitor into this custody system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in all public buildings including airports; criminal penalties to $1,000 and private bounty suits; documented arrest under a comparable law; bans in many other divisions.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Statutory exemptions (chaperoning, emergencies); 29+ divisions without bans; not documented for this division.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal exposure: every use of a public facility during transit is a potential trigger, enforced by private bounties without state initiative.

care_services.exposure: Care for minors banned in 27 divisions including this one; national insurance-reimbursement rule proposed; hospitals subpoenaed for minor-patient records nationally.
care_services.protection: Division district court injunction blocking the minor-care ban; adult visitors' medication access not documented as restricted.
care_services.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces the ban's edge; litigation status unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders frame gender ideology as threat; counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; teachers criminalised for facilitating minor transitions; division bounty law invites citizen enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined; division non-discrimination law since 2020; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing licenses bounty enforcement and facility policing; enjoined measures remain contested and partially operative.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor accompanying a guardian faces birth-sex school/public facility rules, criminalised social transition facilitation by teachers, and records subpoenas; guardian could face investigation exposure.
minors_guardians.protection: Division injunction on the care ban; municipal conversion-therapy bans; adoption and surrogacy equality are resident-facing only.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor's facility use and any school or clinic contact trigger the same bounty and enforcement architecture.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented for this division beyond the restroom arrest; national hate-crime coverage exists but 37 divisions lacked bias statutes (2019); division hate-crime law excludes gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; division public-accommodation non-discrimination enforcement since 2020.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse is partial and unevenly documented; not shown reaching visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No remedy shown changing the division facility law; suit pending; enforcement data, bounty-suit counts, custody-placement practice for visitors all unrecorded.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, ACLU litigation, appellate reversal of one marker ban, state injunction on care ban — courts sometimes work for trans people here.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions (bounty frequency, border treatment of matching foreign passports) lighten weight but do not offset the documented universal exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar core: unremedied birth-sex facility rule applied to visitors including airports, upheld institutions, polite society. This jurisdiction is harsher: bounty suits, criminal penalties, licence invalidation, documented arrest, and national entry-document refusals with foreign-citizen detentions push below 0.35-A.

0.55-C has familiar gender-diverse roles and a dead-letter statute with no universal exclusion. Here the exclusion is universal, enforced by bounty, with documented arrest — a tier-1 feature that 0.55-C lacks, placing this materially lower.

0.25-D pairs birth-sex facility/ward rules with recurrent police stops and fraud threats. This case has comparable facility exposure plus bounty privatisation and national custody abuse, but stronger partial recourse (injunctions, non-discrimination law, hate-crime statute) and no documented recurrent police extortion — sits slightly above.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a hostile national document and speech framework interacting with an aggressively enforced division facility law. The traveller's journey concentrates exposure at airports — the very buildings covered by the birth-sex facility mandate — while entry screening adds document-scrutiny and fraud-ineligibility risk, and any escalation routes into a custody system with documented abuse of trans detainees. The bounty mechanism makes facility exposure enforceable by any stranger, and a real arrest shows the law operates. Courts provide partial, slow, unresolved relief; no remedy reverses the operative rules. Weighted: tier-1 universal exposures dominate, with moderate mitigating institutional recourse and no organised street targeting documented — 0.32, harsher edge of the 0.35 tier.
